title: Phase II study of conformal hypofractionated radiotherapy with concurrent gemcitabine in muscle-invasive bladder cancer
journal: Journal of Clinical Oncology 2011; prospective single-arm phase II study
population: 50 patients with T2–3 N0 M0 transitional-cell muscle-invasive bladder cancer after TURBT and MRI staging; post-treatment cystoscopy available in 47.
treatment: Gemcitabine 100 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8, 15 and 22 with conformal radiotherapy 52.5 Gy in 20 fractions over 4 weeks. Chemotherapy stopped for RTOG grade 3 bladder or bowel toxicity.
comparator: None. Prospective single-arm phase II study; no randomized comparator.
summary: All 50 patients completed RT; 46 tolerated all four gemcitabine cycles. Forty-four (88%) achieved complete endoscopic response. At median follow-up 36 months, 3-year CSS was 82% and OS 75%; 32 of 36 survivors had a functional intact bladder. Four underwent cystectomy; two treatment-associated deaths and one late bowel resection were reported.

absoluteEffect.absoluteBenefit: Not estimable; single-arm phase II outcomes only.
absoluteEffect.toxicity: Four patients stopped gemcitabine early for bowel toxicity; two treatment-associated deaths; one bowel resection for late toxicity.
absoluteEffect.nnh: Not applicable; no comparative harm estimate.

clinicalInterpretation: GemX is a prospective phase II bladder-preservation regimen using weekly low-dose gemcitabine with 52.5 Gy in 20 fractions. It demonstrated promising response and survival estimates but cannot establish superiority over cisplatin or 5-FU/mitomycin C chemoradiotherapy.
criticalReview: Single-arm n=50; median follow-up 36 months. 44/50 complete endoscopic response (88% as reported); 3-year CSS 82%, OS 75%. All completed RT; 46 completed all four gemcitabine cycles. Four underwent cystectomy, two treatment-associated deaths and one late bowel resection. No comparative NNT/NNH.
